evidence_signals.title: EU AI Act Becomes Enforceable Law
evidence_signals.content: The EU implemented the world's first comprehensive AI Act, placing strict systemic risk regulations on foundational models. The heavy compliance burden forced tech giants to geofence their AI deployments, fracturing the global internet.

modules.novelty_rationale: Represents the first binding systemic divergence in consumer and enterprise frontier AI deployment, turning hypothetical digital sovereignty and 'splinternet' concerns into legally mandated architectural geofencing.

modules.velocity: Accelerating into a structural macro-financial transmission phase as mega-scale stablecoin reserves cross the $100B threshold in short-term sovereign paper, superseding localized exchange insolvency risks with bilateral run contagion between crypto liquidity pools and prime sovereign debt markets.

evidence_signals.title: SEC Approves Spot Crypto ETFs
evidence_signals.content: Following massive institutional pressure, the SEC approved spot Bitcoin ETFs, instantly deeply integrating highly volatile crypto assets into traditional Wall Street retirement funds and banking balance sheets.

evidence_signals.title: SEC Files Lawsuit Against Major Crypto Exchange Binance
evidence_signals.content: The SEC sued Binance and its founder for operating an unregistered exchange, offering unregistered securities, and mismanaging customer assets. The high-profile regulatory crackdown severely restricted cryptocurrency market liquidity and institutional trust.

evidence_signals.title: FTX Exchange Insolvency Triggers Crypto Contagion
evidence_signals.content: The sudden collapse of FTX, a dominant cryptocurrency exchange, revealed multi-billion dollar fraud and balance sheet holes. The crisis wiped out billions in retail assets, triggered direct traditional bank run contagion, and froze digital liquidity.

evidence_signals.title: Stablecoin Tether Discloses $100B in US Treasury Backing
evidence_signals.content: Tether reported its fiat-peg assets grew to over $100B, largely comprised of short-term US Treasury Bills. The report highlighted how stablecoins have integrated traditional sovereign debt with decentralized crypto assets, creating systemic circular risk.

modules.novelty_rationale: While crypto assets have existed for over a decade, direct programmatic integration into institutional retirement pools and regulated bank balance sheets bridges previously segregated risk pools into mainstream financial stability channels.

The regulatory green light eliminates structural barriers between volatile speculative digital assets and conventional financial infrastructure, creating cross-market contagion channels across retirement systems, prime brokerage, and commercial bank balance sheets.
Update Reasoning: The SEC enforcement action against Binance directly attacks the primary global offshore liquidity engine for digital assets. This crystallizes systemic legal and counterparty risks, abruptly dampening institutional allocation velocity and erecting formidable regulatory inertia across non-compliant digital asset market structures.
Update Reasoning: The sudden collapse of FTX confirms that centralized, un-segregated crypto conglomerates present acute systemic counterparty risks. The discovery of multi-billion dollar fraud and sudden balance-sheet holes immediately destroys market liquidity, accelerates regulatory crackdowns, and demonstrates direct contagion to traditional banks supporting digital asset rails.
Update Reasoning: Tether's milestone disclosure of over $100B in assets heavily concentrated in US Treasury Bills transitions digital asset contagion from a speculative crypto-native liquidation spiral into a systemic non-bank shadow-banking vulnerability. Any severe de-pegging or run on the stablecoin now carries direct liquidity spillover risk into short-term sovereign money markets via forced asset liquidations.

evidence_signals.content: A cargo ship power failure led to the collapse of a critical bridge, entirely blocking a major US port. The infrastructure failure severely disrupted auto and coal supply chains, adding another vector to the global logistics crisis.

modules.novelty_rationale: While transport disruptions are historically common, modern ultra-large commercial vessels interacting with aging, non-redundant civil infrastructure create instantaneous, severe single-point-of-failure shocks across specialized industrial and energy supply chains.

scenarios.title: Unrealized Duration Mismatches and Digital Contagion Cascade
scenarios.narration: In the initial weeks following a sudden monetary tightening shock, severe duration mismatches and unhedged mark-to-market securities depreciation compound credit losses across depository institutions, driving capital adequacy stress into regional banking portfolios with commercial real estate exposure [e1]. Simultaneously, the revelation of latent mark-to-market balance-sheet insolvencies triggers viral depositor coordination and instantaneous balance-sheet drainage via hyper-velocity digital bank runs [e2], while non-bank financial intermediaries experience refinancing distress and credit model impairment that spill over to prime bank counterparties [e3]. Over the following quarters, deteriorating conditions in regional commercial real estate compound further mark-to-market securities depreciation across depository institutions [e5] and transform latent appraisal declines into realized loan loss provisions, depleting Tier-1 regulatory capital reserves against an impending maturity cliff [e4]. Concurrently, non-bank refinancing distress feeds back into prime banking portfolios, reinforcing duration stress [e8]. The accelerating digital bank runs prompt state-brokered rescue acquisitions by global systemically important banks, heightening sovereign concentration risk and moral hazard [e6], while 24/7 high-speed settlement conduits between fiat institutions and digital asset exchanges propagate contagion into institutional digital assets [e7]. As the crisis deepens, the maturity cliff continues converting appraisal declines into regulatory capital depletion within regional banking [e9], and continuous digital asset settlement channels provide feedback that intensifies hyper-velocity deposit runs [e11]. Furthermore, the concentration of sovereign liquidity absorption within offshore stablecoin reserves and synthetic digital dollar instruments begins eroding US sovereign debt credibility and fiscal governance [e10]. Ultimately, this sovereign debt credibility strain feeds directly back into institutional digital asset conduits via offshore reserve and synthetic dollar dependencies [e12].
scenarios.counterfactual_assumption: A sudden, severe tightening shock generates acute unrealized mark-to-market losses across bank portfolios, simultaneously exposing asset-side duration mismatches and triggering viral, digital-speed liability drainage.
scenarios.novelty_element: The bidirectional feedback loop between high-velocity digital asset settlement channels and traditional fiat bank runs, culminating in sovereign debt governance strain.
scenarios.trigger_signal: Latent unhedged duration exposure in fixed-income bank portfolios coupled with rapid digital deposit flight mechanisms.
scenarios.dynamic_weights_utilization: Transmission strengths are the composite of Phase B'sweights ({'empirical': 0.5, 'narrative': 0.2, 'institutional': 0.3}). buffering-polarity edges attenuated x0.4.

scenarios.title: Bifurcated Semiconductor Mercantilism and Critical Input Feedback
scenarios.narration: Following an initial sudden disruption in sovereign semiconductor mercantilism and tech stack bifurcation, transmission channels bifurcate across financial and resource sectors in the first weeks. Capital market exposure to concentrated compute providers escalates state-driven export restrictions and retaliatory mercantilist bans, transmitting severe stress to AI hardware concentration and equity index stability [e1]. Simultaneously, geopolitical fragmentation weaponizes upstream raw mineral refining monopolies, directly stranding and strangling downstream advanced lithography and semiconductor fabrication infrastructure [e2]. Over the following quarters, these vulnerabilities feed back into the core geopolitical tension. Strains in hyper-concentrated AI hardware equity exposures intensify state incentives to enforce additional export curbs and retaliatory bans, reinforcing sovereign tech bifurcation [e3]. Concurrently, bottlenecks arising from critical mineral refining weaponization further constrain fabrication and lithography, compounding state-driven tech stack fragmentation and pushing the sovereign semiconductor sector to full stress capacity [e4].
scenarios.counterfactual_assumption: A sudden stress shock of intensity 0.7 hits sovereign semiconductor policy, precipitating immediate bilateral export controls and technology stack bifurcation.
scenarios.novelty_element: A direct reflexive feedback loop where capital market sensitivity in hardware equities and mineral weaponization simultaneously re-amplify the initial geopolitical technology shock to its theoretical ceiling.
scenarios.trigger_signal: High capital market concentration in specialized compute providers alongside sovereign concentration in upstream mineral refining.
scenarios.dynamic_weights_utilization: Transmission strengths are the composite of Phase B'sweights ({'empirical': 0.5, 'narrative': 0.2, 'institutional': 0.3}). buffering-polarity edges attenuated x0.4.

scenarios.title: Synthetic Fraud Transmission: From Corporate Treasuries to Algorithmic Contagion
scenarios.narration: In the initial weeks following a sudden shock to corporate treasury vulnerabilities, synthetic multimodal impersonation is weaponized to bypass enterprise authorization protocols and compromise institutional digital keys [e1], while high-fidelity audio and video cloning scales from corporate spear-phishing into macro monetary authority manipulation [e2]. Over the subsequent month, compromised custodial architectures expose institutional settlement and custodial clearing infrastructures to access-control exploitation and liquidity freezes [e3]. Concurrently, synthetic monetary disinformation injects market-moving falsehoods directly into unverified algorithmic execution models, triggering immediate flash drawdowns [e4]. As digital asset distress institutionalizes, the direct connection between primary sovereign liquidity absorption, offshore stablecoin reserves, and synthetic digital dollar instruments begins eroding US sovereign debt credibility and fiscal governance [e5]. Simultaneously, high-speed digital settlement conduits facilitate 24/7 run contagion across digital asset exchanges and fiat banks [e6], while algorithmic fragility amplifies software repository poisoning across concentrated market-making APIs into intraday clearing and settlement standstills [e7]. Over the following quarters, sovereign debt liquidity stress feeds back into institutional digital asset risks [e8]. The compounding digital bank runs force state-brokered rescue mergers of distressed lenders into mega-institutions, inflating moral hazard and sovereign risk buffers [e9] while feeding persistent run contagion back into digital asset platforms [e10]. Finally, third-party infrastructure freezes reinforce systemic AI dependencies and algorithmic market fragility [e11].

scenarios.novelty_element: The cross-domain transmission where synthetic corporate fraud evolves simultaneously into wholesale monetary disinformation and sovereign liquidity strain via stablecoin reserve conduits.
